Measured data

Depth & deficiency register — all 32 clubs

The brief asks the system to know when a defense or an offense is running a 2nd, 3rd or 4th string body in place of a starter. Before this page the root register could answer that for 4 of 32 clubs (data/depth_charts.json charts KC, GB, NE, DET; the other 28 were left blank and flagged as FL-10). This page closes it to 31 of 32, using the only official chart that exists for a club — the one its own site publishes — joined to the official league injury report.

On this pageWhat this page is, in one sentenceThe two sources, and why twoCoveragePer-club roll-upWhere a starter is actually missingWhere a starter did not practiseFull register — every group on every chartEvery depth slot, 1st to 4th stringThe refreshed injury report this join was built onWhat this page still cannot tell you

What this page is, in one sentence

Every position group on every club depth chart, with the starter's official practice and game status beside it, and the name of the man the club would have to turn to next.

The two sources, and why two

InputSourceWhat it provesTier
Depth slot (1st / 2nd / 3rd / 4th string)the club's own official site, e.g. patriots.com/team/depth-chartthe order the club itself printsB — official club site, not league-operated
Practice and game statusnfl.com/injuries (Week 10, read 2026-11-13)the league's own filingA — official league

nfl.com/teams/<club>/depth-chart returns 404. That was verified in an earlier session and published as FL-05. There is no league-operated depth chart to download, so the club's own page is the best official source that exists — and the site says so on every row rather than pretending otherwise.

**Every one of these charts is labelled unofficial by the club that prints it.** Most are compiled by the club's communications staff. They can lag a coaching decision by days. That is the single biggest limitation of this page and it is not smoothed over anywhere below.

How the join works, in the one place it can go wrong. A chart and an injury report name the same man differently — the Patriots' chart prints Kevin Byard III, the league's report prints Kevin Byard. The join is a normalised exact match first and a unique last-name match inside the club second; it never guesses across clubs and never resolves an ambiguous name. Every row therefore carries both spellings: projected_starter is what the club printed, starter_injury_name is what the league printed, and scripts/verify_s745.py re-checks every one of the 159 matched starters against the report they came from.

One row per club. "Chart = no" is Houston: the page exists and is linked, but the chart on it is an image, so zero rows could be transcribed from it. Counts are of position groups, not players: a club printing three wide-receiver lines has three WR groups. DNP and Limited describe the man the club lists first, using that club's own order.

Week 10 read on 2026-11-13, 296 rows across 26 clubs, plus two explicit "No Injuries Reported" markers for LAC and BAL so that "declared none" is never confused with "absent from the file" (FL-01). Each row links the player's own nfl.com profile.

What this page still cannot tell you

  1. How good the replacement is. A chart gives an order, not a talent gradient. Turning "2nd string left tackle" into a point value needs snap counts and play-by-play, which this repository is not entitled to store (Q-02).
  2. Whether the chart is current. 26 of the 31 charts print no date at all (FL-39). Five do: GB, LV, SF and TEN all 10 Nov, and CHI 31 Oct — thirteen days old when this session read it. For the other 26 clubs the register cannot tell you whether the chart is from Tuesday or from October, so it does not pretend to.
  3. Anything about Houston (FL-37). The page exists and is linked; the chart on it is an image. A third-party site publishes a full Texans chart, and it is deliberately not used here — importing it would put a value on this site that no official page confirms.
  4. Where a club prints no first string at all, the register says nothing. Two groups — NYJ DL and PHI DT — have a blank top cell on the club's own chart. Their "depth reached" and "next man up" columns are blank rather than promoted from the second line, because a second-string body is only a replacement for a starter if the club printed a starter.
  5. Whether a 2nd stringer is also the starter somewhere else. Several clubs list the same man first in one group and second in another (Rock Ya-Sin, Jack Cochrane, Anthony Bradford, Kitan Oladapo, Alontae Taylor, Cam Hart, Tacario Davis, Carson Vinson, Ryan Neuzil, Tanoa Togiai, Walter Rouse, Kyle Williams, Barion Brown, Jeremiah Wright, Tyjae Spears is listed jointly). Those are printed as the club prints them and are not de-duplicated, because collapsing them would be an inference about role.
  6. Which man actually takes the field. A chart is an ordering, not a lineup, and two clubs print things no second official page explains: the Eagles' chart names Tanner McKee as its first quarterback and does not print Jalen Hurts anywhere, and it names Jonathan Greenard as a co-first-string at both edge positions (FL-40). Both are reproduced exactly as printed.
  7. Special teams. Not charted here — the brief asks about offense and defense.
